html:
SMTO-EXE-0008 — You stopped this task

GUID: f7ef9770-7d38-448c-9e50-5a341ca9b93e
Slug: user-cancelled
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO stopped the task because Stop was selected. Steps that finished before that stay done; stopping doesn't undo them.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Expand the stopped task in the conversation and look at which steps finished and which never started. Stop only halts the remaining work; changes made by finished steps are still in place.
  2. If a step was cut off midway, check its result yourself, for example whether the file or setting it was changing looks right. A step stopped partway may or may not have made its change.
  3. Only if you still want the unfinished part done, send a new message in the conversation describing just what's left. SMTO won't restart stopped work on its own, and asking only for the rest avoids repeating finished steps.

What success looks like

  • The task shows as stopped, and you can see which steps finished.

If it still fails

  • If the task keeps showing Stopping… for a long time, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't assume stopping reversed any changes; check them first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Work was halted by a user Stop (cancellation token, saved stop record or abandonment state); per-operation receipts record which operations completed, stopped or never started.

What this means

  • The owning cancellation token, saved stop record or abandonment state prevented continued work or requested termination of existing work. Separate receipts determine which operations had started, stopped or already completed. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • The owning cancellation token, saved stop record or abandonment state prevented continued work or requested termination of existing work. Separate receipts determine which operations had started, stopped or already completed.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the stop state together with each owned operation's start, completion and cancellation receipts.

How to fix it

  • No corrective action is required for this informational outcome.
  • No fix is required. Inspect the run's per-operation receipts to see which operations completed, were cancelled or have outcome_unknown before starting conflicting work; cancellation does not roll back completed effects and the run is never restarted automatically.

Retry and execution caution

  • Do not restart automatically. Inspect the retained outcome and start further work only when the user intends it.

How to verify the fix

  • Every affected operation has a settled result or an explicitly retained unknown outcome before conflicting new work.

What not to do

  • Do not automatically restart cancelled work or assume cancellation reversed earlier effects.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
